solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of journey by ship leaderless crew ruined – most of us are meant to hear this (12, two words)

definitions.text: most of us are meant to hear this

indicators.note: a group without its leader has lost whoever stands at the front, so the opening letter goes
something ruined has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a stage is one leg of a journey
taken as written
taken as written, before its first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A sea voyage goes wrong when the crew loses its captain, with a cryptic aside about what the audience hears.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'crew' loses its leader; 'ship' stays whole, and the two together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's loud aside meant to be heard by the audience but supposedly not by others on stage, so most listeners are intended to catch it.

clue.text: Floral spikes grooms fixed round soft saddle

indicators.note: being fixed round something means being set about it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a sice (or syce) is an Indian word for a groom who tends horses
a pad is a soft, treeless saddle

explanation.surface: Stable hands fitting a padded saddle onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sice is an Anglo-Indian word for a groom; its first letter sits outside the saddle, the rest after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spadices is the plural of spadix, the fleshy flower spike of plants such as arum lilies.

clue.text: Alternative to crystal ball? Rating: satisfactory

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor, and a rating is a naval sailor below officer rank
OK means acceptable or satisfactory

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's crystal ball gets a lukewarm review: merely satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like a score to go with 'satisfactory', but it is the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarok is a variant spelling for tarot cards, which fortune-tellers lay out instead of gazing into a crystal ball; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Tawdry MG car Ricky scrapped around life's end

definitions.note: read as a noun: Chambers gives tawdry as showy trumpery or cheap finery

indicators.note: a scrapped car is broken up, so its letters are taken apart and rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept
the rearranged letters go around the single letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the last letter of life

explanation.surface: Ricky's flashy MG sports car is sent to the scrapyard when it reaches the end of its life.
explanation.walkthrough: MG is a British sports car marque. The rearranged letters give GIMCRACK...RY with E dropped in: GIMCRACK(E)RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrackery is showy, worthless ornament, the same cheap finery that tawdry names when used as a noun.

clue.text: Cyclist round Germany? One employs cogs regularly

indicators.note: the first word is put round the second, which sits inside it

blocks.note: a wheeler is one who rides a wheeled machine such as a bicycle
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A cyclist touring Germany, plus a hint at bicycle cogs used regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cogs' suggests gear wheels, but cog is an old verb meaning to cajole or cheat by flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: To cog is to wheedle or coax deceitfully, so someone who regularly cogs is a coaxing flatterer.

clue.text: Actor offering help for those finding movement difficult

definitions.text: help for those finding movement difficult

blocks.note: first meaning: Jeremy ..., the English film and stage actor

blocks.clueFragment: help for those finding movement difficult
blocks.note: second meaning: leg braces, metal supports strapped to weak legs

explanation.surface: A performer helps out people with mobility problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg irons, or calipers, are metal braces that support weak legs when walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a well-known actor, and irons are also the metal leg supports that help people who struggle to walk.

clue.text: Coin, part of nose-piece that's turned up

indicators.note: the letters wanted are only a portion of the following words, sitting inside them
in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen in the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: A coin forming part of a nose-piece, perhaps on old armour, that has been bent upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency unit of Mexico and several other Latin American countries.

clue.text: Poll, one notoriously washing hands after minimum of exposure

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least of it, just its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of exposure
Pontius Pilate washed his hands to disclaim responsibility for Jesus's death

explanation.surface: An opinion poll, Pilate-style, with someone washing their hands of the matter after barely any exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like a vote, but here it is the verb meaning to crop hair; 'after' puts PILATE behind the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To poll is to cut off the hair of the head, and to epilate is to remove hair, so both verbs mean stripping hair.

clue.text: Changed one's mind? Rough, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word is judged on how it is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: rude in the sense of crude or roughly made

explanation.surface: Second thoughts described as a rough process.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair: regretting something is close to wishing you had decided otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, and regretting a choice is a looser way of saying one has had a change of heart about it.

clue.text: Devotee of Rome rudely person holds silly

indicators.note: one piece holds the other, gripping it inside

blocks.note: per. is the dictionary abbreviation for person
apish means foolish or affected, like an ape's behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone devoted to Rome is rudely called silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' belongs with the definition, marking the word as an insult; it is not a signal to rearrange 'person'.
explanation.definitionFit: Papisher is an old, hostile term for a Roman Catholic, a follower of the Pope in Rome, so 'rudely' marks it as an insult.

clue.text: Setting out to punt round Tweed's mid point, here's some fishing tackle (7, two words)

indicators.note: setting out letters means laying them out anew in a different order
the middle point of a word is its central letter, the one kept
the rearranged letters go round the kept letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the middle letter of Tweed

explanation.surface: Someone setting off to punt on the River Tweed brings fishing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is a Scottish border river, which suits this Scots word for a net.
explanation.definitionFit: A pout-net is a Scots name for a funnel-shaped fishing net, so it counts as a piece of angling equipment.

clue.text: Queen comprehends what's untamed in chaos, predating our planet

indicators.note: letters in chaos are in disorder and must be put into a new arrangement
to comprehend is to include, so the first piece takes the second inside

blocks.note: Queen Anne, British monarch 1702 to 1714
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A queen grasps the wild chaos that existed before the Earth formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Antemundane means existing before the creation of the world, so it describes a time earlier than this planet.

clue.text: 'Car club accepts caravanner,' one's noticed with a sniff

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
a Rom is a Romany, traditionally a travelling caravan dweller

explanation.surface: A motoring club welcomes a caravan owner as a member.
explanation.walkthrough: A(ROM)A: the club's two letters split around the traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell, the thing a person detects by sniffing.

clue.text: Luckless Scot that is having to trail behind college staff

blocks.note: dons are university or college teachers
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: An unlucky Scot trailing behind the college staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is part of the definition, saying the word is Scots, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Donsie is a Scots adjective meaning unlucky or ill-fated, so luckless in Scots usage.

clue.text: Monkey, male, gives you a squirt

blocks.note: the douc is a colourful langur monkey of Indochina
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A male monkey sprays water at a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A douche is a jet of water directed at the body, which is a squirt in plain terms.

clue.text: Without number one receding group died

indicators.note: something receding moves backwards, so the next word is read from right to left

blocks.note: 'un' is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good un'
a lot is a group or batch of things
d. is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Number one in a band drops back as the group dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' acts on 'group' alone; the dialect 'un' for one, as in 'a good un', stays the right way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Untold means too many to be counted, so it describes something beyond any number.

clue.text: Path no longer in use, ivy bush enveloping centre of spurway

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, which is the one kept
to envelop is to wrap around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a tod is a bushy clump, especially of ivy
the middle letter of the seven in spurway

explanation.surface: An old bridle path whose middle stretch is overgrown by ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: A spurway is an old word for a bridle path, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Trod is an obsolete noun for a trodden path or track, so it is a footway no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: Bird from street protected by shopkeeper, given lift

indicators.note: something protected is kept safe inside a guard, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upwards so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a trader is someone who buys and sells goods
ST is the abbreviation for street, written here as it reads before the turn

explanation.surface: A bird from the street is sheltered by a shopkeeper who gives it a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird of the thrush family with a reddish tail.

clue.text: One known for rambling with less and less on top

definitions.text: with less and less on top

blocks.note: first meaning: Clare ..., the BBC broadcaster who presents the walking programme Ramblings

blocks.clueFragment: with less and less on top
blocks.note: second meaning: losing hair from the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' suggests long-winded talk, but it is country walking; Clare Balding has long presented BBC Radio 4's Ramblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare Balding is famed for her walking show, and someone whose hair is thinning has steadily less on top.

clue.text: Yield from cash crop takes off in the grass

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, enclosed within it

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
to take off someone is to mimic them, which is what an ape does

explanation.surface: A crop of grass grown for money is harvested and taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' means imitates here, not removes. R(APES)EED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapeseed is the seed harvested from oilseed rape, a major cash crop pressed for oil.

clue.text: Last bit of humour drained from bodily duct

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter, the one taken
something drained from a container is let out of it, so the letter is removed

blocks.note: the final letter of humour
carnal means of the body or flesh

explanation.surface: The last of a bodily humour drains away through a duct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humour' recalls the four medieval bodily fluids, but only its final letter is used; 'bodily' is the word losing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal in anatomy is a tube-shaped passage, such as the ear canal, which is a duct.

clue.text: Heat and leave simmering? Have a ——, not overcooked (7, two words)

indicators.note: simmering letters are bubbling about in the pot, so they come out in a new order
the blank dash shows a phrase being struck out, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written, the full stock of letters
taken as written, the letters to be crossed out

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: heat the pasta, leave it simmering, and keep it firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash after 'Have a' marks those letters as deleted from 'Heat and leave'; the seven letters that remain are then stirred into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente describes pasta or vegetables cooked only until firm to the bite, so stopped short of overcooking.

clue.text: Themes in novel, first of them set in Louisiana

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, the one taken
something set in a place is placed inside it

blocks.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Louisiana
Emma is Jane Austen's novel
the opening letter of them

explanation.surface: Themes in a novel set in Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an anagram signal but is a book title. L(EMMA+T)A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemmata, plural of lemma, are the subjects or headings of a text, its themes or arguments.

clue.text: Voted in strike, and other things included, all retrograde

indicators.note: something included is placed within another word
retrograde means moving backwards, and 'all' says the whole build is read in reverse

blocks.note: dele is the proofreader's instruction to strike out
etc. abbreviates et cetera, 'and other things'

explanation.surface: Workers voted for a strike, among other things, and it all went backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it is the proofreader's instruction to delete; the insert goes in after its first letter before everything is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone elected has been chosen by ballot, so they were voted into office.

clue.text: Lacking ice, a fruit drink to skip?

definitions.text: Lacking ice, a fruit drink to skip?

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
juice is a drink pressed from fruit
lep is a Scots and dialect form of leap, to skip or jump

explanation.surface: Someone skips the ice in a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue sketches a sweet drink as well as building it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet, often fruit-flavoured drink, a mild syrupy beverage one might take without ice.

clue.text: Five hundreds? Twice that, with rest to follow

blocks.note: five hundred is D in Roman numerals, and twice that is a thousand, M
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Doubling a number of hundreds and then taking a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the count is of fish: herrings were traded by this Scots measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A mease is a Scots measure of herrings, traditionally five hundred fish, a quantity rather than a number.

clue.text: Have a rinse up north in basin with 14

indicators.note: only the letters lying in the tail of the word are taken, not the whole of it

blocks.note: the last three letters of basin
14 is the answer to 14-across, whose first letter joins the string

explanation.surface: In the north someone rinses off in a basin with a squirt of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of basin and the 14-across answer, a squirt of water, so the cross-reference must be solved first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sind is a northern English and Scots verb meaning to rinse or wash out.

clue.text: Historical wimple come to light, without red binding

indicators.note: without here means minus, so the letters named are taken away

blocks.note: something revealed has come to light
the letters of red forming the outer binding, two at the front and one at the back

explanation.surface: An old nun's headdress brought out of its red wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: RE...D surrounds the answer like a binding, and removing it leaves the old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Veale is Spenser's spelling of veil, and a wimple is a veil-like head covering of the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Better rooms round bishop's place, furnished in the old style

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, enclosing it

blocks.note: in Scots, the ben is the inner or better room of a cottage
a see is the seat of a bishop's authority

explanation.surface: Superior rooms around a bishop's residence, done out in antique style.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Scots but-and-ben cottage, the but is the outer kitchen and the ben the better inner room. BE(SEE)N.
explanation.definitionFit: Beseen is an archaic word meaning well-appointed or equipped, so 'furnished' in an old usage.

clue.text: Sound of horn number one one tone above tuning note, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, something rising goes upward, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: number one is a nursery euphemism for passing water
orchestras tune to A, and a whole tone above A is B

explanation.surface: A car horn sounding a pitch just above an orchestra's tuning note.
explanation.definitionFit: A beep is the short high sound a car horn makes.

clue.text: Trumpeter maybe showing off when king's gone

indicators.note: once the king has gone, its letter is taken out

blocks.note: swank is ostentatious display
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A trumpet player shows off once the monarch has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' looks like a musician but is a kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpeter is a large North American species of swan, so it is one example; 'maybe' flags that.

clue.text: Desk 'furniture' I had wrapped in ribbons

indicators.note: something wrapped in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: ties are strips used to bind, like ribbons
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Desk accessories that someone had tied up with ribbons.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks admit that desk tidies are hardly furniture. T(ID)IES.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk tidy is a container for pens and clips, the kind of minor equipment found on a desk.

clue.text: Pen empty, half ewes, half rams, wandering fold

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its inside, leaving only the outer letters
half a four-letter word keeps two of its letters, here the front half
letters wandering stray from their places and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the outside letters of pen
the first half of ewes
the first half of rams

explanation.surface: An empty sheep pen, with the flock half ewes and half rams straying from the fold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a sheepfold, completing the farm picture, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap is to wrap something up, which is to fold it around or envelop it.

clue.text: Much-abused princess, one appearing in Hamlet?

indicators.note: something appearing in another thing is found inside it

blocks.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so a Dane
a means one

explanation.surface: A wronged princess turns up in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests a role in the play, but it stands for the prince's nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Danaë was a princess locked away by her father and visited by Zeus as a shower of gold.

clue.text: Glitter surrounding Republican presenting struggle for Trump

indicators.note: one piece surrounds the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: to spangle is to glitter or sparkle
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Political glitz surrounding a Republican, giving Donald Trump a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Trump' signals an American word, since Trump is American, not a battle for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprangle is a US dialect verb meaning to sprawl or struggle, so it is the American word for this effort.

clue.text: Head and tail of porcupine: fear the end after playing around with quills

indicators.note: the head and tail of a word are its first and last letters
the second piece comes after the first in the answer
letters playing around move about freely and take a fresh order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of porcupine
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A porcupine fears the end and fools about with its quills.
explanation.walkthrough: The porcupine's quills fit the surface, but quills here are a bird's growing feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-feathered describes a young bird whose quill feathers have not yet opened, so it is covered in pens, or quills.
